rules.applies_when: the requested workspace contains nested Git repositories or worktrees
rules.check: Resolve every repository root and inspect status before selecting files or deployment targets.
rules.expected: The active project boundary is explicit and unrelated nested repositories and dirty changes are preserved.
rules.fix: Restrict edits and commands to the resolved project; record overlapping dirty changes as a blocker instead of resetting or overwriting them.
rules.validation: Compare repository roots, status output, changed-file scope, and neighboring service state before and after the run.

rules.check: Match the production URL to the exact provider project, branch/environment, web root, service, container, or control-panel target.
rules.expected: The release target is uniquely identified and neighboring projects are outside the mutation scope.
rules.fix: Stop activation when identity is ambiguous; resolve the target from provider metadata and deployment documentation.
rules.validation: Record target identity, project/service name, environment, and affected paths in the release manifest.

rules.applies_when: a release artifact must cross a throttled, unreliable, or size-limited transfer boundary
rules.check: Compare the complete local artifact manifest and SHA-256 hashes with the reconstructed remote release before activation.
rules.expected: Chunked or throttled transfer does not change, omit, or add release files.
rules.fix: Transfer only the scoped artifact in bounded chunks or an archive and retry failed chunks without activating a partial release.
rules.validation: Verify file count, paths, sizes, and SHA-256 parity on both sides before activation.

rules.applies_when: the active deployment model is VPS plus Nginx, optionally with PM2 or systemd
rules.check: Resolve the exact web root, Nginx site file, upstream/port, process name, scoped backup, and health endpoint, then run nginx -t before reload.
rules.expected: Only the requested service is changed and Nginx syntax plus referenced files pass before activation.
rules.fix: Deploy to a temporary scoped release, preserve the previous pointer/configuration, and reload only after nginx -t succeeds.
rules.validation: Verify nginx -t, process health, API health, public HTTP behavior, and neighboring-service non-interference.

rules.check: Run configuration, process, API, and public HTTP checks after activation and compare them with the previous release reference.
rules.expected: Activation failures automatically restore the scoped previous release/configuration and verify the rollback.
rules.fix: Rollback the project-scoped pointer/configuration, re-run configuration validation, and reload only after the rollback passes preflight.
rules.validation: Record failure, rollback location/command, post-rollback health, and final deployment state.

rules.applies_when: source changes and deployment are both in scope
rules.check: Inspect mode flags and user authorization separately for commit, push, merge, and deployment.
rules.expected: A deployment does not implicitly commit, push, or merge Git, and no-push/no-merge gates are honored.
rules.fix: Keep Git publication disabled unless explicitly requested and record the actual Git state in the manifest.
rules.validation: Verify git status, HEAD, upstream, push/merge state, and deployment state separately.

rules.applies_when: an unknown public path supports HTML and Markdown representations
rules.check: Request the same unknown path without Accept, with text/html, with text/markdown, and with a Markdown q-value.
rules.expected: Every unknown representation returns truthful 404/410 status; HTML is useful HTML and Markdown is real text/markdown with public recovery links.
rules.fix: Implement framework/server-native content negotiation without converting unknown paths into a 200 SPA shell.
rules.validation: Run the production response matrix and compare status, content type, body format, and recovery links for every representation.

rules.applies_when: the origin serves different representations based on Accept
rules.check: Compare default/HTML and text/markdown responses for the same URL, including q-values and direct .md siblings.
rules.expected: HTML is returned by default, Markdown is returned only when negotiated or explicitly documented, and both preserve the intended status.
rules.fix: Correct the origin/framework negotiation logic and content type without relying on an untested server default.
rules.validation: Verify Content-Type, body format, status, direct sibling behavior, and cache separation in production.

rules.applies_when: response representation or compression varies by request headers
rules.check: Inspect Vary and repeated cached responses for Accept and Accept-Encoding variants.
rules.expected: Vary includes Accept when representations differ and includes Accept-Encoding when compression differs; cached HTML and Markdown do not cross-contaminate.
rules.fix: Correct origin/CDN cache keys and Vary headers, then purge only the scoped affected cache when authorized.
rules.validation: Run fresh HTML, Markdown, q-value, and compression requests and compare headers, content types, bodies, and cache state.

rules.applies_when: a login, account, admin, checkout, or other private route is reachable over HTTP
rules.check: Request the route without authentication and inspect status, redirects, response body, and robots directives.
rules.expected: Private content is authenticated or denied, does not expose data, and carries noindex protection where the response can be crawled.
rules.fix: Use authentication and project-native meta/X-Robots controls; never rely on robots.txt as the privacy boundary.
rules.validation: Test unauthenticated and authorized behavior without recording credentials or private response bodies.

rules.applies_when: the canonical brand or product identity is clear from truthful project evidence
rules.check: Compare brand naming in title, visible header/footer, Open Graph, application name, schema, About/contact/trust links, and canonical apex domain.
rules.expected: On-site entity signals are consistent, truthful, crawlable, and tied to the canonical domain.
rules.fix: Normalize only source-backed on-site signals and add missing project-native Organization/WebSite/SoftwareApplication data when truthful.
rules.validation: Run a cross-page entity audit and inspect raw production HTML/schema.

rules.applies_when: on-site brand signals are present but external search visibility or authority is weak, generic, delayed, or conflicting
rules.check: Run at least one current external search source when available and classify on-site signals, indexing delay, naming conflict, and external authority separately.
rules.expected: The report does not treat on-site changes as proof of authority and external work remains a human/credential-dependent decision.
rules.fix: Improve truthful on-site signals automatically; batch Search Console, Bing, listings, press, and legitimate external-link actions for human input.
rules.validation: Record external source/date and the exact classification and decision-table row.

rules.applies_when: a supported post-deployment rescan, inspection API, or public crawl mechanism exists
rules.check: Determine whether a bounded rescan can be executed for affected routes after verified deployment.
rules.expected: The run performs the rescan when authorized and available, or records why it was unavailable; a request is not reported as an indexing outcome.
rules.fix: Run one bounded supported rescan and record mechanism, scope, date, response, and limitations.
rules.validation: Separate rescan request evidence from later indexing/citation observations.

rules.applies_when: a run changes source, configuration, deployment, or production behavior
rules.check: Inspect the machine-readable manifest for every material finding and release state.
rules.expected: Each material change records check, expected, change, local verification, production verification, rollback note, scope, and status without secrets.
rules.fix: Create or complete the scoped change manifest before reporting completion.
rules.validation: Parse the manifest and compare file/route/release records with Git and deployment evidence.

rules.check: Inspect the selected mode before release activation.
rules.expected: Source validation may run, but no provider, server, CDN, bucket, container, or control-panel activation occurs.
rules.fix: Keep deployment state as not activated and report the exact artifact and pending production checks.
rules.validation: Verify provider/server audit logs or command plan show no activation and manifest records no-deploy.

rules.check: Inspect Git mode gates before any publication command.
rules.expected: No Git push occurs; local commits are optional and deployment is not used as an implicit publication path.
rules.fix: Do not invoke push; record HEAD, upstream, and the unpushed state in the manifest.
rules.validation: Compare local HEAD with remote refs and confirm no remote ref changed during the run.
